clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old male presented with left-sided flank pain, nausea, and vomiting after a near fall with twisting. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast revealed left renal non-enhancement, secondary to suspected acute traumatic left renal artery dissection. Heparin anticoagulation was initiated for renal salvage. The patient was transferred for a higher level of care, where an angiogram showed a complete lack of flow to the left kidney. Ultimately, the patient required a nephrectomy due to renal necrosis.
